Trump Defends $5,000 ‘Dividend’ for Americans, Says GOP Must Win Congress to Deliver Checks

September 10, 2026 at 11:45 pm
0
>>Follow Matzav On Whatsapp!<<
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 5:06
Instaread

President Donald Trump defended his proposal to send $5,000 payments to every adult American citizen, arguing that the plan would be made possible by the nation’s economic performance and tariff revenues — but only if Republicans maintain control of both chambers of Congress in November’s midterm elections.

In an interview with Fox News host Laura Ingraham, Trump explained why he has tied the proposed “Trump dividend” to Republican victories in both the House and Senate, contending that Democrats would be unable to produce the economic growth needed to support the payments.

“Because – they can’t – I’ll tell you what, because the Democrats can’t do it,” Trump told host Laura Ingraham. “Because with them, it’s negative growth. with us, it’s so positive.”

“We’re taking in $21 trillion. No country has ever taken in anywhere near that,” the president added. “That’s four-five times more than the next. That’s all because of that beautiful word you and love more than most others – tariffs.”

Trump first unveiled the proposal Wednesday night during the Republican Party’s midterm convention in Dallas, where he told supporters that Americans would receive the $5,000 payment if the GOP emerges from the November elections with control of both the House and Senate.

“I can make this promise to you, and here is my promise,” he said. “If the Republicans win the House of Representatives and the United States Senate, both of them, because of our economic — tremendous economic success like in history, we’ve never had anything like what’s happening.”

Trump compared the proposed payments to a company distributing profits to its shareholders.

“But because of our tremendous strength and success economically — I will issue a dividend to every adult citizen in the United States of America for $5,000. Very much like a successful company will do a cash distribution to its shareholders,” Trump added.

The President said recipients would be required to spend the money inside the United States and has pointed to revenue generated by his tariff policies as a source of funding. The proposal, however, would require congressional approval, and independent estimates put its potential price tag at roughly $1.2 trillion. Reuters reported that the Congressional Budget Office says tariff collections during the current fiscal year totaled about $167 billion, substantially less than the estimated cost of the proposed payments.

Republicans currently hold a narrow majority in the House, making the fight for control of Congress a central focus of the party’s Dallas gathering.

Trump again highlighted the amount of investment and revenue he says his economic policies have generated while speaking with Ingraham.

“So, we’re taking in $21 trillion. Nobody – no country has ever taken in anywhere near that. It’s four or five times higher than the next one,” Trump said.

“All because of that beautiful word that you and I love more than most others: Tariffs,” he added.

The proposed dividend has already generated debate in Washington over its cost and economic impact. Some Republican lawmakers have expressed reservations about adding more than $1 trillion in federal spending, while others have embraced the idea and are considering legislation that could put the proposal into effect. Democrats have criticized the election-linked pledge.

During his address in Dallas, Trump also acknowledged the longstanding difficulty presidents face in midterm elections, when the party controlling the White House has historically tended to lose congressional seats. After telling the audience that he’s “doing a great job,” Trump questioned why strong presidential performance does not necessarily translate into midterm victories.

“But I say, why is it that, no matter how well you’re doing, we see not a president — Democrat or Republican — almost never wins the midterms?” Trump said.

He then urged Republican voters to approach November’s congressional races as though his own name were appearing on their ballots.

“We’ve got to change that because we have something going that’s so good we can’t let that string be broken. So, I’m asking you to pretend that I’m on the ballot. I’m on the ballot, just one more time.”

Any $5,000 payment program would ultimately need congressional authorization. Questions also remain about how the government would finance a program costing more than $1 trillion at a time when the federal deficit is projected to exceed $2 trillion. Supporters have pointed to tariff revenue and economic growth, while critics — including some Republicans — have raised concerns about the potential effect on the national debt and inflation.

The White House also promoted the proposal Thursday, portraying it as a way for Americans to share directly in the administration’s economic policies.

“Last night, President Donald J. Trump unveiled the Trump Dividend — a historic $5,000 cash payment to every adult American citizen, made possible by the strength of the American economy under his leadership. The announcement is the latest proof that President Trump does what the so-called ‘experts’ say cannot be done: he delivers for the American people.”

“The Trump Dividend depends on President Trump and Republicans. Democrat control means America loses — and working people pay the price,” they added.
